Source reads "no less than forty years ago"; the candidate's "forty years before" moves the time anchor from the speaker's present to the visit. "ago" is plain modern English and needs no change; restore it.

No content lost. Two small drifts from the source: "a great many Whales" is lowercased (the brief says a rendered paragraph follows the source's capitalization), and "beating the sea before him" becomes "ahead of it", which drops the masculine personification that the other extracts keep ("his mouth" in extracts.33, "his head" in extracts.30). Minimal fix: restore "Whales" and "him" and, for agreement, use "This one came" (the source says "This came").
"the more thankless you will go forever" keeps the old idiom 'go thankless' (= remain unthanked) in scrambled order; a first-time reader and a listener must reread it. Minimal fix keeps the sense.
"horse-whales" stops a modern reader and nothing nearby says what they are; Ohthere's horse-whales are walruses (hence the valuable teeth). Brief accurate gloss, once.
"Several whales have come in on this coast (Fife) in the year 1652": present perfect with a specific past date is not modern English grammar and trips the reader; simple past.
Broken quote: the paragraph ends the quotation ("...could not be avoided." —) but never opens it. Every other prose extract opens with a straight double quote.
